newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis find caves at Jewish settlement site.
newsitem.headline: Israelis find caves at Jewish settlement site.

text.p: Israeli authorities said they had found three caves at a disputed Jewish settlement site in Arab East Jerusalem but insisted building would go ahead even if it turned out they contained ancient Jewish graves.

Housing Ministry adviser Moshe Elat said on Thursday the discovery would not delay construction of the Jewish settlement at Jabel Abu Ghneim (Har Homa in Hebrew) which has triggered Palestinian protests and plunged peace moves into crisis.
Ultra-orthodox Jews have in the past protested at sites where building is carried out on ancient Jewish graves, delaying construction.

"There are three caves. We're not sure if they're burial caves. The caves will be checked but that certainly doesn't require halting work," Elat told Reuters. He said the caves were discovered on Wednesday.
A member of the Atra Kadisha group for the preservation of Jewish holy sites said even if burial caves were discovered, provisions could be made to allow construction without "disturbing the dead".
"A year ago a survey was done but nothing clear was discovered. Checks will be made but there are always ways to get around the issue," said David Schmidl of Atra Kadisha.
Israel's Antiquities Authority denied there were burial caves at the site but said ancient human bones are often dug up during construction in the Holy Land.
"It is reasonable to assume that sooner or later we will find human bones," said authority spokeswoman Osnat Gaoz.

Israel's groundbreaking last week for a Jewish settlement at the site has sparked daily clashes between Israeli troops and Arab stone-throwers. Palestinians view East Jerusalem, captured by Israel in 1967 and annexed, as the capital of a future state.
